content.overview: If any of the provisions of sections 139 to 146 (both inclusive) is contravened, the company shall be punishable with fine which shall not be less than twenty-five thousand rupees but which may extend to five lakh rupees and every officer of the company who is in default shall be punishable with fine which shall not be less than ten thousand rupees but which may extend to one lakh rupees. Where the auditor has contravened any of the provisions of section 139, section 143, section 144 or section 145, the auditor shall be punishable with fine which shall not be less than twenty-five thousand rupees but which may extend to five lakh rupees or four times the remuneration of the auditor, whichever is less. Higher consequences apply where the auditor has contravened knowingly or wilfully with intention to deceive.
content.glance: Contravention of ss. 139–146 attracts company and officer fines; auditor contravention of ss. 139, 143, 144 or 145 attracts auditor fines, with higher consequences for knowing or wilful deception.
content.study:
## Section 147 — Punishment for contravention

**Company and officers.** Contravention of any of sections 139 to 146: company fine not less than ₹25,000 and up to ₹5 lakh; every officer in default fine not less than ₹10,000 and up to ₹1 lakh (and imprisonment where the section provides).

**Auditor.** Contravention of section 139, 143, 144 or 145: fine not less than ₹25,000 and up to ₹5 lakh or four times the auditor's remuneration, whichever is less.

**Knowing or wilful deception.** Higher consequences including refund of remuneration and damages to the company, statutory bodies, members or creditors, as the section states.

This note is a focused study aid; the topic remains under source and current-law review.

hypotheticals.question: Does section 147 replace section 447 for auditor fraud?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 147 is the chapter-specific penalty. Where the fraud definition under section 447 is met, that provision may also apply; do not treat section 147 as displacing it automatically.

misconceptions.correction: Ordinary contravention and knowing/wilful deception with intent to deceive have different consequences under the section.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does section 147 punish?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Contravention of sections 139 to 146 by the company and officers, and contravention of sections 139, 143, 144 or 145 by the auditor, with higher consequences for knowing or wilful deception.
